source_name: NBS Politika oversightu NBS (oversight policy PDF)
why_relevant: The Bank Board-approved oversight policy for payment systems and payment instruments — the doctrinal document behind NBS supervision of SIPS/TARGET2-SK and card/e-money instruments. Explains scope, escalation and assessment cadence.

source_name: NBS Prístup do platobných systémov NBS (SIPS / TARGET2-SK access rules, July 2025)
why_relevant: Access conditions document for non-bank PSPs joining SIPS/TARGET2-SK (applications open from 6.10.2025). Directly signals a structural market opening — new participant categories in SK clearing infrastructure, i.e. new competitors and new integration/vendor demand.

source_name: NBS Aktuality (regulator news feed)
why_relevant: Regulator news stream announcing licensing milestones, market openings and sector counts (e.g. 'six licensed crypto-asset providers operate in Slovakia', 'NBS opens payment systems to non-bank PSPs'). Fastest signal of structural change in the SK payments competitor set.

source_name: NBS Dohľad kryptoaktív (MiCA / CASP supervision)
why_relevant: MiCA supervision section covering CASP authorisation, notification duties and the participation of incumbent financial institutions in crypto-asset services. Adds an adjacent-competitor layer to the SK payments map (six licensed CASPs as of the 2025/26 transition).

source_name: NBS Správa o inovačnom hube a regulačnom sandboxe (annual innovation hub report)
why_relevant: Annual report on the NBS innovation hub and regulatory sandbox — describes the kinds of fintech propositions, business models and technologies firms brought to the regulator. A rare regulator-side window on the SK fintech pipeline before those actors appear in registers.

source_name: NBS Správa o činnosti útvaru dohľadu nad finančným trhom (financial market supervision activity reports)
why_relevant: Annual supervision reports summarising licensing activity, on-site inspections, sanctions and thematic reviews per sector including payment services. Gives the volume and nature of regulatory action against SK payment actors — useful as case-study material and as a competitor-health indicator.

source_name: NBS Legislatíva — metodické usmernenia a stanoviská útvaru dohľadu
why_relevant: Searchable repository of NBS supervisory methodological guidance and opinions, e.g. the 1 April 2025 opinion of the Financial Technologies and Innovation Department on safeguarding payment-service users' funds. Reveals which practices the regulator is actively policing — a leading indicator of compliance-driven vendor demand.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 11/2023 — statistical reporting on payment services (cards, terminals, fraud)
why_relevant: Defines the quarterly reporting templates resident PSPs must file on payment transactions, cards, terminals by device type and payment schemes. Establishes exactly what card/terminal market data exists at NBS — the schema behind any published SK acquiring/terminal statistics, which is directly relevant to a POS/terminal vendor lens.

source_name: NBS Registre portál (registre.nbs.sk)
why_relevant: Separate NBS registry application hosting professional-competence registers of institutions and persons. Secondary for payments, but a useful pointer to training/certification providers and to individuals moving between SK financial firms.

source_name: NBS legacy site www.nbs.sk/sk/platobne-systemy (archival payment-systems pages)
why_relevant: Pre-redesign NBS site tree still surfacing in search results; holds older oversight and payment-system pages and historical SIPS/TARGET2-SK material no longer linked from the current site. Useful for time-series and for recovering documents whose new URLs moved.

source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa – Finančné ukazovatele / Investori (financial indicators & annual reports hub)
why_relevant: Official disclosure hub of Slovakia's largest bank; hosts výročné správy, IFRS statements and Pillar 3 / NBS Opatrenie 16-2014 disclosures where outsourcing arrangements, digitalisation capex and transformation programmes are described. SLSP procurement is private, so this is the compliant channel for vendor/partner mentions.

source_name: Erste Group Bank AG – Financial Reports (parent-group filings)
why_relevant: Erste Group's consolidated annual reports and investor presentations describe group-wide IT/digital programmes (George platform, Erste Digital hub, core-banking consolidation) that are executed at Slovenská sporiteľňa; often name technology partners and quantify transformation spend at a level SLSP's local report omits.

source_name: Erste Digital GmbH, o. z. Slovakia – company site and Slovak commercial register entry
why_relevant: Erste Group's captive IT company has a registered Slovak branch (historic name Erste Group IT International GmbH, o. z. Slovakia). It reveals how much of SLSP's IT is insourced to the group vs. bought from third parties — decisive for sizing the addressable vendor opportunity — and its own filings/job ads expose the technology stack.

source_name: Tatra banka – Výročné správy archive (annual reports, SK and EN)
why_relevant: Tatra banka publishes a deep multi-year PDF archive under a stable URL pattern (/files/archiv/financne-ukazovatele/vyrocne-spravy/ for SK, /files/archiv/en/about/economic-results/annual-reports/ for EN). The reports carry digital-transformation narratives, outsourcing notes and related-party IT service disclosures with RBI entities.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International – Results & Reports (parent-group filings)
why_relevant: RBI's group reports describe the CEE-wide core-banking and payments consolidation (a group 'T24 hub') under which Tatra banka implementations run; the group level is where platform choices and rollout sequencing across Slovakia are stated.

source_name: Temenos success story – Raiffeisen Bank International / Tatra banka Payment Hub
why_relevant: Vendor-published case study that names Tatra banka (Slovakia) as a Temenos Payment Hub implementation inside RBI's group core-banking hub. Vendor case studies are the counterpart channel to bank disclosures and confirm incumbency at a named Slovak bank — a direct competitor-mapping datapoint.

source_name: PosAm – Tatra banka IT outsourcing reference (End User Services)
why_relevant: Slovak systems integrator's own reference page documenting that it won a Tatra banka tender for end-user IT services and took over the contract from a prior foreign provider. Concrete evidence of a competitor's incumbency and of how these private-bank tenders are run and disclosed only vendor-side.

source_name: VÚB banka – Pillar III / Zverejňovanie informácií podľa Opatrenia NBS č. 16/2014
why_relevant: VÚB publishes semi-annual Pillar 3 disclosures under NBS Opatrenie 16/2014 with a highly regular URL pattern (year/period encoded). Operational-risk and outsourcing sections here are the compliant window into third-party dependencies at Slovakia's second-largest bank.

source_name: VÚB banka – Ročná finančná správa / Annual Report (SK and EN)
why_relevant: The full ročná finančná správa carries the management report chapters on digitalisation, IT investment and outsourcing to Intesa group service entities, plus related-party disclosures that expose intra-group technology service flows.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo – Investor Relations subsidiary financial reports (VÚB volume)
why_relevant: Intesa republishes each subsidiary's annual financial report in a dedicated 'bilanci controllate' folder, giving an English, machine-fetchable copy of VÚB's report plus the group annual report describing the technology/IT strategy imposed on Slovak operations.

source_name: ČSOB (Československá obchodná banka, a.s.) – Výročná správa / Annual Report document library
why_relevant: Bilingual SK/EN annual reports served from a stable document-library path (/documents/11005/98584/), covering the bank and, separately, ČSOB Poisťovňa. Contains the management report on digitalisation, the KBC group service arrangements and the ČSOB/365.bank combination in Slovakia.

source_name: KBC Group – Investor Relations results, quarterly reports and company presentations
why_relevant: KBC's quarterly reports and company presentations break out the Czech Republic and Slovakia segment and describe the digital-first / Kate AI assistant programme and the ČSOB–365.bank combination in Slovakia — the single most consequential SK banking-technology event to track for vendor implications.

source_name: 365.bank – Výročné správy (annual reports incl. ESEF)
why_relevant: 365.bank (ex-Poštová banka) publishes consolidated and individual annual reports, including ESEF/XHTML packages. Its digital-only rebuild and the pending combination with ČSOB make its disclosures the richest SK-domestic source on a live core/digital-platform transformation.

source_name: Prima banka Slovensko – Výročné správy
why_relevant: Mid-sized retail bank (ex-Dexia banka Slovensko) with a long PDF archive back to at least 2017 and a 2025 ročná finančná správa. Smaller banks disclose IT/branch modernisation in more concrete, less boilerplate language than the systemic four, and are the likelier greenfield vendor opportunity.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (ORSR) – bank and IT-subsidiary entity extracts
why_relevant: Authoritative registry establishing legal form, branch status and statutory bodies for every actor in this cell — essential to tell a Slovak a.s. (SLSP, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank, Prima banka) from a pobočka zahraničnej banky (UniCredit SK, mBank SK), which determines what each is obliged to disclose locally.

source_name: FinStat.sk – Slovak company financials and register aggregator
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator that normalises RÚZ + ORSR data per IČO, surfacing revenue/headcount trajectories for bank branches and for IT vendors serving banks (e.g. Erste Digital's Slovak branch). Faster triage layer than the raw registers, and it preserves historic names (Poštová banka, Dexia, BRE Bank) which are essential search aliases.

source_name: Národná banka Slovenska – Pilier III: výkazníctvo a zverejňovanie (supervisory disclosure guidance)
why_relevant: The supervisor's own pages define what Slovak banks must disclose and when (Opatrenie NBS č. 16/2014 and successors), which tells the collector exactly which document types exist, their cadence, and the correct Slovak search terms. It anchors the whole cell's collection calendar.

source_name: NBS CERI – electronic collection of regulated-issuer information (ceri.nbs.sk)
why_relevant: NBS's central store for regulated-issuer filings; a search hit surfaced an XHTML (ESEF) filing for an SLSP group entity under an LEI-based path, indicating that Slovak bank and bank-subsidiary annual financial reports land here in structured form — far better for automated named-entity extraction than scraping bank PDFs.
